store_data.about_the_game:
Command your party. Conquer the dungeon together.

Rally the Parties is a semi-real-time tactical RPG where time only flows while your active character is acting. You direct the battle through high-level orders, and your party members act autonomously based on their assigned policies. You can switch between characters at any time to take direct control of any role.
Melee, ranged, support, lockdown, flanking — seven character classes each bring unique combat techniques, and your tactical options shift dramatically depending on how you combine them. Orchestrating synergy between party members is the key to success.

Features

  • Semi-real-time combat: Time only advances while your character is acting — a distinctive system that lets you think carefully before committing to your next move.
  • Seven classes, seven roles: Swordfighter, Axe Warrior, Scout, Archer, Fire Mage, Water Mage, and Healer. Each has its own attack range and special abilities, and the way you mix them reshapes your strategy.
  • Lead through directives: Issue party-wide orders such as Attack, Defend, Rally, or Retreat. Your companions interpret your intent and act on their own judgment.
  • Recruit and expand: Talk to NPCs you encounter in the dungeon and build a party of up to eight. Different combinations open up entirely different approaches.
  • Multiple parties exploring at once: You're not the only group in the dungeon — several NPC parties roam and explore on their own. Sometimes you cooperate, sometimes you compete; their presence gives the adventure life and unpredictability.
  • Roguelike stakes: One defeat ends the run. Every attempt invites you to rethink your party, equipment, and tactics on the path to the Demon Lord at the deepest floor.

Screenshots

Origins

In my youth, I was struck by Ali Baba (Starcraft, 1985) — an RPG where you switched between multiple characters as you played — and was further captivated by the arcade game Gain Ground (Sega, 1988), which built its design around the strategic use of distinct characters with unique abilities. That sense of fascination has never faded.
In the years since, tactical RPGs and MMORPGs flourished, and games featuring parties of cooperating characters became commonplace. But none of them quite captured what I was looking for. The ideal game system remained a recurring daydream — never something that felt within reach to actually build.
Then came the recent rise of generative AI, which suddenly made it possible for an individual to produce a game at a quality previously requiring a full studio. Sensing that this might be the last opportunity to bring a long-held idea to life, I finally began development. Rally the Parties is the result.

Who this game is for / About Early Access

This game is made for players who:
  • Enjoy game systems built around strategically managing multiple characters
  • Are drawn to experimental games that step outside familiar genre conventions
  • Are looking for a gameplay experience they haven't had before
Rally the Parties launches in Early Access. The core combat system, party formation, dungeon exploration, and the full path to the Demon Lord battle are all in place — even now, the game offers a complete, self-contained experience. store_data.detailed_description:
Command your party. Conquer the dungeon together.

Rally the Parties is a semi-real-time tactical RPG where time only flows while your active character is acting. You direct the battle through high-level orders, and your party members act autonomously based on their assigned policies. You can switch between characters at any time to take direct control of any role.
Melee, ranged, support, lockdown, flanking — seven character classes each bring unique combat techniques, and your tactical options shift dramatically depending on how you combine them. Orchestrating synergy between party members is the key to success.

Features

  • Semi-real-time combat: Time only advances while your character is acting — a distinctive system that lets you think carefully before committing to your next move.
  • Seven classes, seven roles: Swordfighter, Axe Warrior, Scout, Archer, Fire Mage, Water Mage, and Healer. Each has its own attack range and special abilities, and the way you mix them reshapes your strategy.
  • Lead through directives: Issue party-wide orders such as Attack, Defend, Rally, or Retreat. Your companions interpret your intent and act on their own judgment.
  • Recruit and expand: Talk to NPCs you encounter in the dungeon and build a party of up to eight. Different combinations open up entirely different approaches.
  • Multiple parties exploring at once: You're not the only group in the dungeon — several NPC parties roam and explore on their own. Sometimes you cooperate, sometimes you compete; their presence gives the adventure life and unpredictability.
  • Roguelike stakes: One defeat ends the run. Every attempt invites you to rethink your party, equipment, and tactics on the path to the Demon Lord at the deepest floor.

Screenshots

Origins

In my youth, I was struck by Ali Baba (Starcraft, 1985) — an RPG where you switched between multiple characters as you played — and was further captivated by the arcade game Gain Ground (Sega, 1988), which built its design around the strategic use of distinct characters with unique abilities. That sense of fascination has never faded.
In the years since, tactical RPGs and MMORPGs flourished, and games featuring parties of cooperating characters became commonplace. But none of them quite captured what I was looking for. The ideal game system remained a recurring daydream — never something that felt within reach to actually build.
Then came the recent rise of generative AI, which suddenly made it possible for an individual to produce a game at a quality previously requiring a full studio. Sensing that this might be the last opportunity to bring a long-held idea to life, I finally began development. Rally the Parties is the result.

Who this game is for / About Early Access

This game is made for players who:
  • Enjoy game systems built around strategically managing multiple characters
  • Are drawn to experimental games that step outside familiar genre conventions
  • Are looking for a gameplay experience they haven't had before

store_data.about_the_game:
A world held together by old oaths and older wounds.

IconicQuest is a pixel-art, top-down MMORPG built for people who remember when the genre respected your time. Real-time skill-based combat. A shared persistent world. Loot that means something. No pay-to-win, no auto-battle, no skip button. Built solo, in the open, by one developer.

Combat you have to actually play.

You swing, they swing back. Accuracy ratings, evasion, weapon velocity tiers, attack speed — every hit is calculated, every miss is yours to learn from. Different mob families have different patterns. You learn their patterns. You stop dying as much. That's the game working correctly.

Position matters. Buffs matter. Preparation matters.

A world with places that mean something.

Teon Town sits at the center of four roads. Each one leads somewhere specific — a wasteland where the creatures have started moving with purpose, a frozen north sealed by an inscription someone chiseled out, a half-buried fortress where a watcher named Gareth doesn't say much.

You find things by going places. Every landmark was put there for a reason the world has mostly forgotten. Some of those reasons are still waiting.

Gear that means something.

No junk drops. No rarity inflation. When a weapon drops, you remember it. Crafting requires a recipe scroll, the right materials, and the right station. Enchant your gear from +1 to +16 — succeed and it gets stronger and starts to glow, fail and you don't.

You'll use the same sword for a long time. That's not a flaw. That's the point.

Real multiplayer. Not singleplayer with online tacked on.

A shared persistent world. Party system. Player nameplates. Open-world grinding zones. Group dungeons. PvP. The kind of MMO where the people around you are people, not bots, and where going somewhere dangerous together is an agreement, not a matchmaking queue.

The promise.

  • No pay-to-win, ever. Cosmetics and convenience only. Power is earned in the world.

  • Real-time, skill-driven combat. No auto-play, no skip buttons.

  • Loot has weight. No junk drops, every item earns its slot, the economy is real.

  • A world worth exploring. Hand-placed, not procedural. Every road leads somewhere.

  • Built alone, in the open. By someone who has spent 22 years playing MMOs and decided the game they wanted didn't exist yet.

Early Access: what you'll find at launch.

  • Real-time combat with multiple mob families and distinct archetypes

  • Open-world exploration with hand-placed zones, towns, and dungeons

  • A starting class system with branching specializations

  • Station-based crafting (anvil, workbench, campfire) with recipe scrolls dropped from mobs

  • Gathering: mining, with herbalism, woodcutting, and fishing on the roadmap

  • Enchanting from +1 to +16 with visible glow tiers and risk of failure

  • Full party system with shared persistent world and player nameplates

  • PvP in designated open-world zones

  • Group dungeons including the Temple of Ice and Fire

  • Quest system with kill, collect, deliver, and dialogue objectives

  • Travel Master NPCs for fast travel between zones you've discovered on foot

Why Early Access.

IconicQuest is built by one developer. Early Access is how the world grows next: more zones, more dungeons, more classes, more depth — built with the people playing it, not in a vacuum. The roadmap is public. The Discord is where it happens first. If you want an MMO that respects your time and your wallet, this is where to start.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Gavel Falls in Gallows & Gold

Sentence the guilty and spare the innocent—or do the opposite. Set in a grim medieval era, Gallows & Gold is a hand-etched judgment simulator where your verdicts carry the weight of life and death. Navigate corruption, law, and your own morality in a world crafted entirely in pen and ink.

The Gavel is Yours.

The King is fading, the treasury is dry, and the people are hungry. You have been appointed to the High Court of Anglia—not to find the truth, but to maintain the peace. In a kingdom where the "King’s Rot" consumes the crown and the Church demands its pound of flesh, justice is a luxury the realm can barely afford.

Key Features

The Weight of Judgment: Every morning, the doors creak open to reveal a new soul seeking mercy or a new villain deserving of the rope. You are the final arbiter. No decision is easy. Review evidence, listen to pleas, and weigh the testimonies of the desperate. Every sentence you scrawl reshapes the kingdom's future—affecting the economy, public order, and your own standing with the crown.

Based on Real History: Preside over trials inspired by actual medieval court records. From frantic farmers accusing their livestock of witchcraft to where pigs were prosecuted for murder, no two cases are the same. You will face the same bizarre dilemmas as judges of the Middle Ages.

Judge the absurd & The Grim: 

Analyse the Evidence: Sift through the Evidence Ledger to find the truth, or ignore it entirely if the bribe is high enough.

Declare the Sentence: One click decides it all. Whether you decide the convict is innocent or guilty, the question is do you let them free or at what length do you punish the guilty? You decide.

The Impossible Balance

Your bench is a scales of three weights: The Crown, The Church, and The Commoners.

 Rule for the King to keep your head, even if the laws grow more erratic.

 Rule for the Priest to keep the Church’s favour, or risk being branded a heretic yourself.

 Rule for the People to stop the city from burning, even if it leaves the royal coffers empty.

Beyond the Courtroom

When the candles low, the trial ends, but the game continues in your Private Chambers.

 Rewrite the Law: Use your Law Ledger to toggle the decrees of the land. Make the "Tax on Bastardy" a reality or mandate archery practice for every peasant.

 Reap the Rewards: Reinvest your gold into the Judicial Estate. Upgrade your execution equipment to ensure "efficiency," or build labour camps to turn convicts into currency.

 Medieval Moral Complexity: Navigate a world of deep political intrigue. Will you uphold the strict letter of the law, or will you accept "gold" to look the other way? In the medieval era, justice is rarely blind, and the truth is often a matter of perspective.

 The Kingdom: Every choice you make carries a compounding weight. Will your judgements lead the land to flourish in a golden era, or spark an immenent demise?

 Branching Narratives: Your verdicts have ripples. Sparing a thief might lead to a rebellion; hanging a saint might lead to a miracle. Witness the long-term consequences of your judgments across multiple playthroughs and endings.

The evidence is thin, the rope is thick, and the King is waiting. What is your verdict?

store_data.about_the_game:
Blackout Protocol is a systems-driven sci-fi survival prototype where you must restore power, stabilise a damaged spacecraft, and bring critical ship systems back online before time runs out.

Restore the Ship

Start with minimal emergency power and bring the ship back online step by step. View the spacecraft from a top-down 3D view while interacting with ship devices, control panels, alerts, and camera feeds.

Use In-World Ship Interfaces

You are aboard a damaged vessel drifting towards danger. The ship is dark, unstable, and running on limited emergency power. To survive, you must inspect ship systems, restore power flow, activate key devices, and bring the vessel back under control before it is too late. The layout is designed to make the ship’s systems readable while keeping the experience focused on restoring power and stabilising the vessel.

Manage Limited Power

Every active system matters. Lights, consoles, batteries, generators, and ship systems all affect the power state, so careless use can slow recovery or leave critical systems unavailable.

Explore a Modular Sci-Fi Vessel

The ship is hand crafted with a mostly intuitive layout where players will need to explore and learn about the different devices and systems on board.

Included Content

Blackout Protocol currently includes one focused emergency recovery scenario designed for a short play session, usually around 5–20 minutes depending on player skill and experience.  You will die.....
(probably)

store_data.about_the_game:
Thick fog blankets the concrete residential blocks, and in the light of a lone streetlamp stands your "fortress" for the summer — an ordinary street kiosk. Uncle Alik has left on business, leaving behind a set of keys, a stack of paper invoices, and a pager. Your first night shift is ahead, and how it goes is entirely up to you.

This is an atmospheric vendor simulator set in the post-Soviet suburbs, where there is no place for rushing. Immerse yourself in the melancholic aesthetics of a bygone era: listen to the monotonous hum of an old refrigerator, count small change, and watch the night life of the foggy neighborhood unfold.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE A KIDNAPPING VICTIM

After a wild party with your coworkers, you wake up in the basement of an old castle — chained like an animal.
Darkness, occult symbols, and the remains of previous victims surround you. Why were you chosen?
Why did the cult single you out? Questions you don’t yet have answers to — and ones you must uncover yourself.

DECIDE YOUR FATE

Will you try to escape the Satanists' lair and find out why you were the victim? Will you save another victim… or only yourself? Or perhaps begin to see the cult from a different perspective? The choice is yours in Sacrificium

YOUR MENTALITY WILL BE TESTED

Every decision you make has consequences. What seems logical at first may lead to unexpected outcomes, and your choices will shape your fate. To survive in this cursed place, you'll have to do things you'd never normally consider — and some of those choices may slowly destroy your sanity. But you are not alone. The whisper in your ears keeps guiding you forward. Is it helping you survive... or have you already lost your mind?

FEATURES

⛧ Psychological horror with multiple endings.

⛧ An interactive text adventure set in the lair of Satanists.

⛧ Choices that affect sanity and health.

⛧ Atmospheric retro-inspired visuals.

⛧ Occult and satanic themes

⛧ An interactive text adventure set in the lair of Satanists.

⛧ Choices that affect sanity and health.

⛧ Atmospheric retro-inspired visuals.

⛧ Occult and satanic themes

store_data.about_the_game:
SINKING INTO THE VOID is a 2D side-scrolling hack-and-slash action game focused on intense battles against powerful enemies.

Players can equip up to three weapons at once and switch between them instantly to adapt to any situation.

Fast-paced combat combines movement, jumping, and dashing with melee attacks, ranged attacks, and abilities.

In addition to guarding enemy attacks, players can perform a precise “Just Guard (Parry)” by blocking at the exact right moment.

A successful parry can stun enemies, reflect projectiles, and completely turn the tide of battle.

Each stage features unique gimmicks and a wide variety of enemies, while boss stages offer even more challenging encounters.

The game also includes time attack elements, encouraging players to refine their routes, optimize their equipment, and push for faster clear times.

Equipment is divided into six slots: Right Hand, Left Hand, Head, Body, Arms, and Legs.

Items come in four rarity tiers: Normal, Rare, Epic, and Legend.

Equipment can also grant a wide range of special effects, such as:

  • Launching fireballs when attacking

  • Increasing damage as HP gets lower

  • Becoming invincible while jumping

By combining these effects, players can create their own unique combat style and build.

Carefully choosing randomly dropped equipment, refining builds, and constantly improving clear records are at the core of the experience.

SINKING INTO THE VOID is an action game designed to keep players saying, “Just one more run.”

【游戏简介】 《六艺：中文填字》不仅是一场考验知识量的头脑风暴，更是一次在指尖静心沉浸的文化巡礼。游戏将经典的汉字填字玩法与极具东方美学的视觉设计深度融合，为热爱文字解谜与百科问答的玩家，开辟了一个古朴雅致、包罗万象的知识世界。

【游戏特色】

📌 以“六艺”为骨，筑万象之基 游戏结构溯源中国古代君子必修的六门功课，构建出“礼、乐、射、御、书、数”六大主题卷宗。

  • 内容恢弘： 涵盖 36 大主题篇章，关卡纵贯古今中外。从历史地理到前沿理工，从诗词歌赋到流行影视，从体育竞技到动漫游戏，知识点无所不包。

  • 挑战升级： 每篇包含至少三个精心设计的填字残局。当你完成前六卷的洗礼，更有终极的第七卷“合”等待开启，挑战你知识储备的极限！

🧩 贴心交互，丝滑解谜体验 为了让玩家专注于思考而非操作，我们设计了极具人性化的辅助系统：

  • 视域聚焦： 当前选中的词条及其对应提示词将同步高亮显示，让你在密集的网格中瞬间锁定目标。

  • 词组连输： 全面支持各类中文输入法的词组连续输入！无需逐个选定方格，输入完整词条即可自动填充，让解谜如行云流水。

  • 温情助攻： 遇到暂时无法攻克的生僻字？点击“提示”按钮即可揭晓。

  • 一键校对： 拿不准填得对不对？随时使用“检查”功能，系统将即时反馈正确性，助你精准破局。

🎨 四季流转，定制视觉美学 游戏内置了“春、夏、秋、冬”四套独具匠心的视觉主题供你自由切换。

  • 从初春的淡绿竹影到凛冬的深邃静谧，每个主题都拥有专属的古典配色与 UI 细节。每一次点击，都如同在宣纸上翻阅一卷精美的水墨画册，让解谜过程成为视觉的享受。

🍃 沉浸式智力禅修 这里没有倒计时的焦虑，没有繁杂的操作负担。伴随着落笔时清脆悦耳的音效，看着错综复杂的网格被正确的字符填满。这不仅是解谜，更是一段属于你自己的、宁静且充满成就感的思维修行。

准备好接受“六艺”的洗礼了吗？落笔生花，就在此刻。

SURVIVE THE GALACTIC FRONTIER Welcome to Aethelgard. You are the commander of an upgradable starship lost in a hostile, resource-rich sector of deep space. Your mission is simple: mine rare ores, trade for powerful technology, and survive the endless waves of elite alien warships hunting you down.

UPGRADE YOUR ARSENAL Start with a basic vessel and transform it into an unstoppable dreadnought. Collect Kyberium and other precious resources from asteroid fields and defeated enemies to purchase devastating laser cannons, heavy shielding, and high-tech engine thrusters.

INTENSE SPACE COMBAT Experience fast-paced, top-down 2.5D space combat where positioning and strategy are everything. Dodge incoming enemy fire, launch calculated counter-attacks, and watch enemy ships explode in spectacular cinematic destruction.

KEY FEATURES:

  • Dynamic Progression: Progress through multiple ship tiers, visually transforming your vessel from a scout to a heavy destroyer.

  • Economy & Trading: Dock at space stations, access the Black Market, and carefully manage your credits.

  • Procedural Encounters: Face off against giant meteors, unexpected ambushes, and heavily armed alien bosses.

  • Cinematic 3D & 2.5D Atmosphere: Enjoy a breathtaking fully 3D environment played from a tactical 2.5D perspective. Marvel at moving starfields, deep space nebulas, dynamic 3D lighting, and stunning particle effects.

The sector is unforgiving. Will you become the ultimate Galactic Guardian?

store_data.about_the_game:
Backrooms: Blackhole is a cooperative psychological horror game for 1–4 players. Somewhere deep within the endless halls, reality begins collapsing into a growing void that consumes light, sound, and everything around it. The deeper you descend, the less the world makes sense — and the harder it becomes to tell what is real.

Play alone or with friends as you explore unstable environments, avoid hostile entities, and uncover the origin of a phenomenon that should never have existed.

Features

  • Dark and oppressive psychological horror atmosphere

  • Online co-op for 1–4 players

  • Proximity voice chat

  • Reactive and unpredictable enemy AI

  • Multiple difficulty modes

  • Stealth-focused survival gameplay

  • Large nonlinear environments with hidden paths and dangers

  • Tension-driven exploration and resource management

  • Dynamic visibility system affected by movement, shadows, posture, and flashlight usage

Important Notes

This game is inspired by the Backrooms concept but presents its own original interpretation rather than strictly following existing community lore. The experience focuses on isolation, fear of the unknown, and distorted environments designed to feel increasingly surreal and hostile.

The game contains flickering lights, disturbing imagery, loud noises, darkness effects, and intense audiovisual sequences that may affect sensitive players.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Last Braincell: Escape is a humorous, asymmetrical multiplayer game in which one player takes on the role of the fugitive, while the others cooperate as the police. The fugitive tries to gather resources, conceal their identity, and reach the escape point, while the officers collect clues, search the area, and coordinate the pursuit.

Main characters:

Fugitive (Orange Braincell)

Clever, chaotic, and definitely way too confident. His goal is to disappear off the map, secure a fake identity, and reach the escape point before the police cut off every possible route. He can improvise, hide in absurd places, and pull off ideas that sound terrible on paper but somehow work.

Police Officer (Blue Braincell)

Alert, stubborn, and fully prepared to search half the map over a single suspicious report. He operates based on clues, tips from civilians, and coordination with other officers. He must quickly assess situations, secure areas, and anticipate the fugitive’s moves before he vanishes across the border. 

Goals in the game :

Prototype build. Release date: TBD. Wishlist now!

store_data.about_the_game:
Idlemoor is a dark fantasy idle RPG set in a persistent online realm of ruined settlements, grim barrows, and slow-burning character growth.

Choose how your character survives: fight enemies, train combat styles, gather resources, craft gear, trade with other players, fight against other players in PvP, and climb the rankings. Progress continues while you are away, but active players can make sharper decisions, react to community events & random events, manage the market, and push deeper into the world.

Core Features

Persistent online progression
Your character keeps advancing over time through server-side saves and account-based progress.

Combat, training, gathering, and PvP battlegrounds
Fight players & creatures, improve combat stats, mine, woodcut, forage, skin animals, and build your character through multiple highly-connected complex gear & stat systems! 

Player economy
Buy, sell, and trade through a shared marketplace where player activity shapes item movement.  Each item is totally unique, and will never drop with identical stats.  Build your character with multiple in-depth skill systems, as well as several stat and gear systems that connect to form a complex meta-game of infinite potential choices!

Community features
Chat with other players, compete on rankings, engage in community events every day, and take part in a persistent realm instead of a purely local idle game.

Idle Pacing
Idlemoor is built for long-term progression: short check-ins, longer grinds, rare drops, and slow accumulation of power.

- Watch money pile up, fade, and get collected

store_data.about_the_game:
Vector Storm is a fast-paced top-down arcade shooter that rewards aggression, precision, and smart builds.

Fight through endless waves of escalating enemies, survive devastating boss encounters, and grow stronger with every

run.

Survive. Build. Repeat.

Each run drops you into an arena that gets deadlier by the wave. Clear enemies to earn credits, spend them in the

mid-run shop on weapons and upgrades, and scavenge gear from fallen bosses. Die, bank your tokens, and come back

stronger.

Build Your Loadout

Equip tiered gear across seven slots — cockpit, wings, boosters, plating, shield, dampener, and weapon bay. Every

piece changes how your ship performs. Stack synergies, push your combo multiplier, and find the build that carries you

deepest.

Five Ships. Five Playstyles.

Start with the balanced Viper or unlock faster, stranger ships as you clear waves. The heavy Bastion regenerates

shields. The Phantom opens with a stealth window. The Ironclad reflects damage back. Each ship demands a different

approach.

Meta-Progression

Tokens earned each run fund permanent upgrades — more health, faster fire rate, bonus starting credits, and more. Sink

enough tokens into the tree and the arena changes with you.

Features

[] Endless wave-based survival with escalating difficulty

[] Seven-slot gear system with tiered boss drops

[] Five unlockable ships with unique passives

[] Deep mid-run upgrade shop

[] Persistent meta-progression across runs

[] Multiple distinct boss encounters

[] 44 Steam achievements

[] Global leaderboards

[*] Procedurally generated adaptive soundtrack
